bull.b: Sustained high-single-digit organic growth across U.S. and international markets indicates broad demand for Stryker’s products. Continued expansion supports operating leverage, strengthens customer and surgeon adoption, and provides a durable base for earnings growth over the next several quarters.

Strong margins and substantial free cash flow demonstrate that Stryker converts its medical-device business into meaningful internal funding. This supports product investment, acquisitions, debt management and shareholder returns while reducing reliance on external financing for continued expansion.

A broad pipeline of launches across robotics, orthopaedics, trauma and surgical technologies can deepen Stryker’s presence in hospital workflows and increase utilization of its installed base. Product innovation also helps defend market position and create recurring procedure-linked demand.

bear.b: Ongoing cybersecurity-related costs and production effects can pressure earnings and operating efficiency beyond the initial incident. Continued remediation also consumes management attention and investment that could otherwise support innovation, commercialization and margin expansion.

The Inari disruption exposes near-term execution and product-availability risk within peripheral vascular, with lost sales and backorders already affecting results. Even if conditions improve by the end of Q3, delayed procedures and customer disruption may weigh on recovery and sales consistency.

bear.t: Meaningful debt and uneven cash conversion
bear.b: Leverage has improved, but sizable absolute debt still requires disciplined capital allocation, particularly as Stryker prioritizes acquisitions. Cash conversion below EBITDA can periodically reduce financial flexibility, limiting the cushion available for investment or unexpected operating pressures.
